title: Read and write decimals to hundredths and name the tenths and hundredths places

lesson.title: Naming the Tenths and Hundredths Places

steps.say: You already know how to colour tenths and hundredths on a hundred grid. Today we learn how to read and write those same amounts as numbers, and what to call each spot after the decimal point.

visual.caption: 47 of the 100 little squares are coloured

steps.say: Here is the rule. The first digit right after the decimal point sits in the tenths place, because it counts big strips worth one tenth. The very next digit sits in the hundredths place, because it counts the tiny squares worth one hundredth. Look at zero point four seven. The four is in the tenths place, and the seven is in the hundredths place.

visual.caption: 4 is in the tenths place, 7 is in the hundredths place

steps.say: Let us read it out loud with money. A sticker at the school store costs zero point four seven dollars. That is four dimes and seven pennies, which is forty-seven cents. So we read the whole number as forty-seven hundredths. We say the digits after the point together, then name the last place we land on.

Now here is the mistake I want you to dodge. If I ask you to write three hundredths, it is very tempting to write zero point three. But that is wrong! Zero point three means three of the big strips, which is thirty little squares. Three hundredths is only three tiny squares, so the three has to sit in the hundredths place. We put a zero in the tenths place to hold that spot, and write zero point zero three.

visual.caption: 3 tiny squares is 0.03; all 30 coloured squares would be 0.3

steps.say: So always check which place your digit lands in. Second spot after the point means hundredths, and it may need a zero in front to push it there.

visual.caption: 0 in the tenths place, 3 in the hundredths place

lesson.answer: First digit after the point is tenths, second digit is hundredths — so three hundredths is 0.03, not 0.3.

practice.question: A little beetle on the school field is six hundredths of a metre long. Write that length as a decimal number, and tell me which place the six is sitting in. Then, for the number zero point eight five, name the digit in the tenths place and the digit in the hundredths place.
practice.answer: The beetle is 0.06 m long, and the six is in the hundredths place (the zero holds the tenths place). In 0.85, the eight is in the tenths place and the five is in the hundredths place.
